name: OSS Showcase
summary: An Agent Skill for maintainers. Build an evidence-backed README, record a reproducible demo, and generate and validate a static GitHub Pages site.
social_tagline: From repository evidence to a README, demo, and project site.
setup: From the folder you want to showcase, install the skill with Node.js and npm available. Choose your agent when prompted.
result: Open a session in the target project. Run $oss-showcase in Codex or /oss-showcase in Claude Code. The current default branch starts by proposing a plan.

sections.title: What does OSS Showcase produce?
sections.body: It helps you prepare a README, a reproducible demo, a static project page, and launch drafts. Public claims and examples come from project files or tests. The static generator stages a reviewed file list before GitHub Pages deployment.

sections.title: What stays under your control?
sections.body: Approve one step at a time or authorize the remaining eligible steps in the plan. Public destinations and payloads need explicit approval. The skill records unfinished work in docs/HANDOFF.md in the target project.

sections.title: Can I review an existing project first?
sections.body: Yes. Use the audit mode for a read-only review of the existing showcase. Use launch mode to prepare channel drafts and publish mode to execute an approved publication.

demo.alt: The Task Counter fixture returns Tasks: 2 before OSS Showcase generates and validates its site.
demo.caption: The fixture outputs Tasks: 2. The generator builds the README and site, then the validator stages only the HTML, CSS, and sitemap.
